title: Illerup Ådal weapon sacrifice — Roman coins among a Germanic war-booty deposit
language_note: Excavation/scholarly reporting in Danish and English (Jørgen Ilkjær's multi-volume excavation publication is the primary academic source); no inscribed regional-language text associated with this find.
date: deposited soon after 205 CE (dendrochronology of shield boards); latest coin minted 187/8 CE
findspot: Illerup Ådal, near Skanderborg, East Jutland, Denmark — a lake/bog weapon-sacrifice site

findspot_places.name: Illerup Adal
findspot_places.note: Confirmed against the Pleiades places snapshot of 2026-08-10 by coordinate — 56.053, 9.939, East Jutland near Skanderborg — feature type 'settlement', attested -30..2099. Pleiades holds no separate entry for Skanderborg; the deposit site itself is what is placed.

original_text_excerpt: Contents include gold, silver, spear shafts, shield boards, ropes, cords, leather, textiles, tools, wooden vessels, spoons, beads, four horses and a cow. The deposit contains 194 Roman denarii, four barbarous imitations, and a sestertius.
original_text_note: Summarized from excavation reporting (Ilkjær) as synthesized on Wikipedia (Roman Iron Age weapon deposits / Illerup Ådal).
notes: Unlike Gudme's trade-linked hoard (scandinavia-02) or Hoby's diplomatic-gift context (scandinavia-01), the Illerup Roman coins arrived as war booty carried by a defeated Scandinavian raiding force — a third, distinct mode of Rome-Scandinavia contact (military/mercenary rather than trade or gift-exchange) worth representing as its own edge type in the Pillar 2 knowledge graph.
